case_title: Anuj Singh @ Ramanuj Singh @ Seth Singh v. The State of Bihar
accused_occupation: Manoj Singh: government service (junior engineer, per defence alibi evidence); Anuj Singh: Not stated
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour; prior enmity over a land dispute
statutory_provisions: Charged: IPC s.307 (with s.34 for co-accused) and Arms Act s.27; finally upheld: IPC s.324 and Arms Act s.27
weapon: Firearms (guns) used by the two appellants; spear and lathi used by co-accused
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; medical evidence (PW-8 doctor); defence alibi evidence (DW-1, DW-2)
aggravating_circumstances: Use of firearms by the two appellants in an altercation over land
mitigating_circumstances: Injuries inflicted on non-vital parts of the body (noted by the Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.307 r/w s.34 (5 years RI, fine Rs.5,000) and Arms Act s.27 (3 years RI, fine Rs.2,000)
high_court_outcome: Conviction under s.307/34 IPC modified to s.324 IPC (2 years RI, fine Rs.5,000); Arms Act s.27 conviction and sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.324 (voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons); Arms Act s.27
neutral_facts: The incident arose from a dispute over a boundary wall on land claimed by the victim. The victim was repairing a mud wall that had fallen in rain, with the help of hired labourers. A neighbour objected to the repair work and said the land was his. A verbal altercation followed. The neighbour went to his house and returned with a second man, both carrying guns. Two other men then arrived carrying a spear and a lathi. The two armed men fired shots at the victim. One shot struck the victim's left leg and another struck the victim's right arm or hand. The other two men then assaulted the victim with a spear and a lathi. On hearing the gunshots, family members and villagers came to the scene, and the four men ran away. The victim was taken to a private clinic. The doctor who examined the victim recorded entry and exit wounds on the right forearm and left leg, with charring of the skin at one site. He stated that all injuries were caused by firearms and were simple in nature. He also stated that tattooing may not appear over a wound if fired from 6-7 feet. Several eyewitnesses, including family members and persons present nearby, testified that the two armed men were present, carried guns and fired at the victim after the altercation. Some witnesses were declared hostile. One of the accused said he was posted elsewhere on duty that day, and a defence witness supported this, but a prosecution witness said he was present at the scene. The investigating officer recorded the victim's statement, visited the scene and noted an ongoing dispute over the land.
offence_severity: Maximum three years, or fine, or both; minimum not stated
physical_harm: Gunshot wounds to the victim's left leg and right forearm (entry and exit wounds, charring of skin at one site); simple in nature
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.307; Arms Act s.27); 2 finally upheld (IPC s.324; Arms Act s.27)
premeditation_planning: Not found; the Court described the firing as arising from an altercation
motive: Prior enmity over a land dispute (accepted by the Court); the altercation concerned preventing the victim from repairing the wall
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent eyewitness testimony placing both appellants at the scene armed with guns and causing the injuries; medical evidence of PW-8 that injuries were firearm injuries
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses found credible despite minor contradictions on timing and injury location; the alibi of one appellant did not inspire confidence
trial_duration: offence: 10.10.1999; trial judgment: 22.12.2006; High Court: 16.01.2018; Supreme Court: 22.04.2022
legal_representation: Accused: Mrs. Anjana Prakash, Senior Advocate, with Anuj Prakash, Ms. Jaikriti S. Jadeja, Prabhat Ranjan Raj and Shantanu Sagar. State: Abhinav Mukerji, Saket Singh, Ms. Sangeeta Singh and Mrs. Niranjana Singh (for the Respondent)
investigation_status: FIR registered 10.10.1999; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; cognizance taken 01.09.2000; committed to Sessions 16.01.2001; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: FIR sent to the Magistrate two days late (12.10.1999); raised by the defence, not decided by the Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.307/34 IPC and Arms Act s.27. High Court: s.307/34 modified to s.324 IPC (2 years RI); Arms Act s.27 upheld. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: The High Court rightly convicted the appellants after analysing the witness statements; no illegality warranting interference
defence_argument: No recovery of gun or bullets; unexplained delay in forwarding FIR; contradictions in witness statements cast doubt on the prosecution story
legal_principle_applied: Minor contradictions do not discredit a witness; medical evidence has corroborative value; ingredients of s.324 IPC (voluntary hurt by dangerous weapon such as firearm) applied; s.27 Arms Act follows once s.324 is established
precedent_relied_upon: Narayan Chetanram Chaudhary & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra (2000) 8 SCC 457
